After BofA Merrill Lynch sounded out Party A in April 2013, Party A made an unsolicited $17-$19 proposal on 06/21/2013, and a new Special Committee launched an outreach to 50 parties on 06/24. Twenty parties signed NDAs, and CSC/Pamplona, Party B and Party C sent preliminary indications around 07/23. Those three and Party A went into a staged second round, with strategic bidders kept from customer data, and all four submitted revised indications on 09/09-09/10. On the request for final indications by 09/18, Party C dropped out, Party A stood at $18-$19, Party B offered $19.00 cash plus options it valued at $21.50, and CSC/Pamplona offered $20.75 with fully committed Pamplona funding. The Committee countered at $21.25, CSC/Pamplona accepted as its last and best offer, and exclusivity was signed on 09/24 and extended on 10/12. The merger agreement at $21.25 cash was signed on 10/14/2013 and announced on 10/15/2013.

cells.Question: Process and round map: is this one process with three rounds (round 1 opening 06/24/2013, round 2 07/25, round 3 09/11), with the 04/08 Party A call and the 06/21 Party A proposal in round 0?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. One process, rounds opening 06/24, 07/25 and 09/11. Most plausible alternative: round 2 opens at the 08/27 letter rather than 07/25, which would remove #24, move #26, #27, #28 into round 1 and make #29 the round-2 opening.
cells.Why, with page: Round 1 opens with the 06/24 decision; outreach followed within days (p. 32). Round 2: four bidders selected into a staged information stage tied to revised offers (p. 33-34). Round 3: the first request for final indications (p. 36). Gaps of two months or more with no acquirer contact: 10/23/2012-04/08/2013 (before any sale step; #1 is a buy-side engagement) and 04/08-06/21/2013. E5: (a) fails, Party A kept in view (pp. 28, 31); (b) fails, gap under three months and no reported end; (c) met, 06/24. So no second process. The 2011-2012 Discussions were a target buy-side effort.
cells.What changes if answered differently: If round 2 opened 08/27, round 1 would absorb the information stage, and Party A's NDA and the access differences would move to round 1. Treating 04/08 as the start of bilateral round-1 negotiation would move #2 and #7 into round 1 and make Party A's bid solicited.

findings.title: R01 decided: bidder-commitment changes as same-price bids
findings.detail: Whether termination-fee and sponsor-guarantee changes communicated at an unchanged price receive separate same-price Bid events or remain dated terms in Notes. Austin decided by whether the term changes the bidder's ability to walk away.
findings.proposed_change: Check the displayed extraction against the decision: the September 21-23 final package and the October 5 and October 8 sponsor-liability proposals are same-price Bids; the October 7 and October 11 target-fee terms stay in dated Notes.

recorded_decision.decision: Bidder-commitment changes (reverse termination fee, sponsor damages cap or guarantee, adding or dropping a financing or closing condition) are same-price Bids carrying the standing price; the target termination fee stays in a dated Note; target requirements on the bidder's commitment are Other material event.

Exit reason: Value at or below market price
